violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.circle_members has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.circle_members FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: Permissive policy grants access to PUBLIC
violations.message: Permissive policy 'directory is public' on public.circle_members grants access to PUBLIC, so anonymous connections are governed by this policy's own clause — its USING for reads, its WITH CHECK for writes (a FOR INSERT policy has no USING at all). Restrict to a specific role (e.g. TO authenticated).

violations.title: Policy expression does not reference any column of the table
violations.message: Policy 'directory is public' on public.circle_members does not reference any column of the table. The predicate is purely session-state — every row is admitted or denied based on configuration alone. Add a row-level condition (e.g. tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')).

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.circle_members is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: Permissive policy USING clause is constant true
violations.message: Policy 'directory is public' on public.circle_members has USING (true), which admits every row to every caller in the role list. Replace with a real predicate or remove the policy.

violations.title: RLS-enabled table has no write-side policy
violations.message: Table public.circle_members has RLS enabled and 1 policy, but every policy is FOR SELECT — no policy covers INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. With RLS enforced and no write-side policy, writes by non-owner roles are denied: INSERT raises a row-violates-policy error, while UPDATE and DELETE silently affect zero rows. If the table is meant to be read-only for these roles (writes done by a table-owning or BYPASSRLS role), allowlist it as 'public.circle_members' in [lint.rules.SEC022]. Otherwise add a policy covering the write commands — a FOR ALL policy, or a FOR INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policy.

violations.title: RLS table has a principal column no policy scopes by
violations.message: Table public.circle_members has RLS enabled and a policy, but no policy references the principal column(s) 'user_id'. Rows are scoped by whatever the policies do key on (often tenant), so users that share that scope can see each other's rows. If this table holds per-user-private data, add a predicate keying on 'user_id'; if it is intentionally shared (a catalogue, a tenant-wide settings table), add it to [lint.rules.SEC027].allowlist.

violations.title: Anonymous read leak (USING is unconditionally true for an unauthenticated session)
violations.message: Policy 'directory is public' on public.circle_members leaks every row to an anonymous session. Under an unauthenticated connection every auth function (auth.uid(), auth.role(), current_setting(), …) returns NULL, and Z3 proves the USING predicate is then unconditionally TRUE for every row (three-valued / Kleene logic) — so the policy reads all rows. Every row is visible unconditionally (the predicate is constant-true under anon — it pins no row column). Gate the policy on a non-null auth check (e.g. `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND <tenant/owner check>`) or remove the inverting disjunct that admits anonymous. This is the semantic form of the SEC004 inverted-auth hole — see SEC004 for the syntactic variant.

violations.title: PostgREST-exposed table readable by a low-trust role
violations.message: Table public.circle_members is in the PostgREST-exposed schema public, grants SELECT to anon, authenticated, and has no effective row filter (RLS is enabled but only a permissive USING (true) policy, which admits every row) — it is directly readable at GET /rest/v1/circle_members by an unauthenticated or any-authenticated request. Enable RLS with a row-scoping policy (or restrict/REVOKE the grant); if the table is intentionally public, allowlist 'public.circle_members' in [lint.rules.SEC049]. (SEC001/SEC003/SEC008 each flag a precondition of this in isolation; SEC049 is the conjunction.)
